status: registered before multi-year data download (2-tile probe only), embedding, training or scoring
motivation: User (2026-09-27): learn 'normal' from multiple years instead of the hand rule. A1b's hand normalisation (divide by the pre-pair change) is the quick version; N1 tests a learned per-location normal model.
data: A1b tiles (KuroSiwo, 26 flood events since 2019). Planetary Computer sentinel-1-rtc, dominant relative orbit per tile, one acquisition per month for 36 months before the event (history), last acquisition <= event-5 d (pre), first in [event, event+12 d] (post); 192x192 at 10 m on the tile UTM grid, VV/VH dB (code/n1_fetch_s1_series_v0.py). Labels only from KuroSiwo masks (evaluation).
embeddings: OlmoEarth v1 Base single-date S1 embeddings, patch 4, identical preprocessing to the KuroSiwo cache; tokens stored at 24x24 (80 m) for all chips and 48x48 for pre/post

model.name: normal forecaster
model.input: for one token location: the previous K=12 monthly embeddings (+ day-of-year and gap in days as features)
model.output: predicted next embedding (mean) and a per-token log-variance
model.loss: Gaussian negative log-likelihood on cosine-normalised embeddings; history months only (event window excluded); tiles split by EVENT into 3 folds, the model scoring an event never saw that event's history in training

score: surprise at the post acquisition = mean over dims of (post - predicted)^2 / predicted variance, given the history up to pre

hand: raw change 1-cos(post, pre) on the same PC RTC chips
hand-normalised change (A1b rule) on the same chips
methods_compared.climatology: 1-cos(post, mean of the same calendar month in the previous years)
external: AlphaEarth raw/normalised and SAR raw/normalised as in A1b (strongest of them)

metrics: T1 tile AUC flood vs dry+perm (primary), flood vs perm; T2 token AUC at 80 m; event-clustered bootstrap (2000)

verdict.learned_normal_helps: n1_surprise - max(hand-normalised, climatology) >= .05 on T1 with CI lower > 0 in >= 2 of 3 seeds
verdict.meaningful_vs_strongest: n1_surprise - strongest of all compared methods >= .05 on T1 AND T2 (CI > 0)
verdict.no_gain: otherwise (reported; the paper then stays with the hand rule / workshop route)

known_limits: PC RTC differs from KuroSiwo GRD processing; all methods in N1 use the same PC chips except the A1b external baselines
flood date = KuroSiwo flood_date (T0: some dates are approximations)
80 m tokens for T2 are coarse
